## [0.36.0] - 2026-09-24

Hovering a `{{variable}}` token now opens its real popover instead of a
separate read-only tooltip, matching Postman's own behavior, and a
collection's export/import round trip carries every field now instead of
losing most of what the UI shows. Also here: deleting from the collection
tree with no confirm dialog, several layout fixes at the app's default
density, and the macOS menu bar's own name.

### Added

- Hovering a `{{variable}}` token now opens the same popover a click does,
  after the usual debounce, instead of a separate read-only tooltip. A click
  on the token itself now only places a text caret in it - editing the raw
  token text no longer needs arrowing in from an edge.
- Deleting a collection or request from the tree runs immediately, with no
  confirm dialog - it was already an undoable soft delete, so the dialog was
  guarding a mistake Undo already covers. A collection with a mock server
  running still asks, since stopping that mock isn't something Undo brings
  back.
- Exporting a bound collection now asks whether to **Keep contract**
  (examples and parameter values only, the existing default) or
  **Write everything**, which writes every field - names, auth, scripts,
  saved examples, even new operations - back into the document's own
  dialect, Swagger 2.0 included. Importing an OpenAPI, Postman or Insomnia
  file now keeps folder nesting and descriptions, collection variables,
  execution settings, GraphQL bodies, digest/AWS/NTLM auth and more that
  used to silently drop on the way in or out.
- An import preview that skips a request now names it, instead of only
  saying how many were skipped.

### Changed

- Error messages, dialog copy and labels throughout the app were rewritten
  against a new writing guide: "can't" instead of "cannot", one settled
  term per concept (like "Vayu's engine" for the sidecar), and plainer
  language in place of jargon and dropped metaphors.
- Settings' backup card is now just called **Backup** - "Workspace" isn't a
  Vayu concept.

### Fixed

- Toasts, the Trash drawer's item names and Settings' header text could
  crowd against the buttons next to them at the app's default density -
  several places were sized off the density setting itself rather than a
  fixed measure, up to 25% narrower than the class name implied. The same
  gap is fixed everywhere else it turned up: menus, popovers, autocomplete
  lists, dropdown floors and skeleton placeholders.
- Hovering one variable and then quickly hovering a different one in
  another editor could close the second popover instead of the first - a
  stale timer from the first was closing whatever was open rather than the
  one it was actually scheduled for.
- The popover for a `{{token}}` in a script or body editor could close
  itself while the pointer was still resting on it, unless you'd clicked
  inside first.
- The popover for a `{{token}}` in a header field or the URL bar could
  flicker instead of opening.
- The macOS menu bar read "Quit vayu-client" instead of "Quit Vayu".
- A DNS failure and a target server breaking the connection (an empty
  reply, a reset, a redirect loop) were both reported as generic
  connection or internal errors instead of naming what actually happened.
- Importing an OpenAPI file from a URL that answered with an error page (a
  404 or 500) blamed the file's format instead of naming the server's
  answer.
- A second delete queued behind one still running could be silently
  dropped, and a failed create, duplicate or delete could leave the Dock
  reading "Not saved" as if an edit were still pending.
- Introspection reported "HTTP 0" as if the endpoint had actually answered,
  instead of naming why nothing came back.
